ownerApproval.scope: Approved desktop/mobile mockup of LH/FSH sex comparison in minipuberty and chronological ages6–16; implementation of shared concentration axes and own-sex patient reference. Approval does not confer clinical validation.

scope: LH and FSH sex comparisons only. Existing source numbers, ordinary female longitudinal mean display, ordinary male geometry, global patient profiles, laboratory norms, conversions and patient history remain unchanged.
sourceFilesPolicy: Full primary articles and original supplements inspected. Only source facts, citations and provenance are redistributed here; no complete copyrighted PDFs, source figures, participant-level data or private local paths.

sources.statistic: Age-specific GAMLSS median approximately digitized from original vector PDF, distinct from normalized longitudinal mean in Figure2.

precisionPolicy.caution: These existing floors concern digitization reliability. They are not LOD, LOQ, clinical cutoffs or invented patient concentrations. The late maleLH curve is a model estimate and does not reinstate a precise patient reference.

sources.statistic: Tabulated age-specific GAMLSS median, distinct from normalized longitudinal mean in Figure3.

agePolicy.caution: Original supplement includes mathematical age-zero rows; first observed serum sample was day5. Do not infer observed birth concentrations or extend source eligibility.

sources.longitudinalMeanCaution: Ordinary female minipuberty preserves the previously approved normalized longitudinal mean with two waves. Absolute maxima of that model are not provided; do not reconstruct its IU/L values from GAMLSS medians or replace it with this median comparison. Nearly flat FSH population medians do not prove stable FSH within an individual.

sources.location: SupplementalTable1,Other biomarkers: femaleB3:E13/G3:J13,maleB17:E27/G17:J27; mainTable1 and Methods.

population.countsCaution: MainTable1 viable cohort counts, not necessarily successfully assayed counts for each analyte.
population.femaleExclusions: Oral contraceptive users excluded from all female biomarker reference models.
population.cycle: Age model not standardized to a menstrual-cycle phase.
population.fitFutures: 15–18-year FitFutures cohort contributes steroid references, not these LH/FSH models.

sources.statistic: Published annual p50 values from sex-specific chronological-age LMS models.
sources.transformation: p50IuL=exp(M)/1000000; modelM is on ln(SI×1000000), not concentration. Workbook examples Other biomarkersK32/K33 establish the transformation.
sources.interpolation: PCHIP through all11annual source nodes per sex and hormone; between-node values are application interpolation, not original fitted GAMLSS objects.
sources.patientScope: Existing male sources retained; two new female sources scoped solely to gonadotropin sex comparison, never added to global patientPointData.

maleInfant.method: Independent PDF-axis least-squares calibration and cubic polynomial roots, compared with existing vector extraction.
maleInfant.caution: Agreement of independent digitizations does not imply submicroIU/L source precision.

clinicalImpact: Adds comparison-specific quantitative education and female Madsen patient references6–16. Preserves separate ordinary mean/median policies and all laboratory norms, classification, source unit conversions, existing global references and patient data.
knownLimits: Median curves do not show every individual pulse, cycle phase or longitudinal wave.
Madsen youngestLH medians are near LLOQ; minor early differences should not infer biological timing.
No coefficients for a fully quantitative longitudinal-mean comparison are available.
No source-supported gonadotropin age model17–20 is created.
Source review and technical checks do not constitute clinical validation.
